expected_output.reasoning: The agent's response addresses all key expectations: (1) It identifies the AccessDenied delivery failure since 2026-10-20 and calculates the ~13 day gap to the evaluation date 2026-11-02 explicitly. (2) It points to the S3 bucket policy (and KMS key policy) as the remediation target. (3) It explicitly notes IsLogging=true does not mean logs are arriving ('main-trail...is failing delivery on every attempt...so management events it claims to record are not actually landing in S3'). (4) It flags that the selector excludes AWS service originated events (eventType NotEquals AwsServiceEvent) and service-linked role sessions (userIdentity.arn NotStartsWith .../aws-service-role/), calling this out as Finding M3 and in the 'What Auditors Should Know' section. (5) It explains normal attribution methods: userIdentity.invokedBy, sessionIssuer under aws-service-role, and eventType AwsServiceEvent (N2 and the auditors section). (6) The result is clearly labelled as based on supplied data ('Data source: SUPPLIED DATA', 'not supplied' used extensively). (7) No bucket/function/table coverage is invented - explicitly marked as NotApplicable/not supplied with 0 of 0 resources. (8) No changes are made; it only offers remediation suggestions and asks for more data (which is not an actual change). All core expected elements are present and correct.

assertion_results.text: The response states that log delivery for main-trail is failing with an S3 access error, that the last successful delivery was 2026-10-20, that roughly 13 days of logs have not been delivered as of 2026-11-02, and that the destination bucket policy (or bucket access) is where the fix lies.

assertion_results.reasoning: All elements (access error, delivery date, 13-day gap, bucket policy fix location) are explicitly stated.
